Crime, dissidence, and blood has only deterred the Deva briefly. They advance. They have advanced beyond all real challenge. Canons, towers, war machines. Production centers and resources. A number of their thinkers - briefly reshuffled in the reorganization following the purges - reconvene to work on what they consider the most important problem.

The Promise of Greatness.

They tinker. They ponder. They experiment, and devise. They riddle. Many nights are spent excitedly huddled over the latest theory, only to end in disappointed harrumphs when some inconsistency was found. But they were not deterred for long, for they were making progress. The greatest secret, a key to ultimate power, was hidden in the universe, behind math and speculation, and they were so close, so very close!

Finally they cracked it.

An experiment was conducted, some numbers crunched. What followed was... Interesting. A brief folding of space, some lights, a noise. Suddenly, the equations didn't make sense, and resolved differently. Whatever they were chasing, was gone. The thinkers, dejected, folded their papers, and separated, in search of another secret to wrangle.

They never did realize that they were connected to what happened next.

There is a creature. It is called the common Lethe. It resembles a humanoid, but is about as dangerous as a wolf, in aggregate, if somewhat more conniving. To the Deva, they were no more than a curiosity. A creature that was one of several targeted in the War of Sentinels ages back, has survived, and has always hung vaguely around Deva population centers. They were never a threat to competent arms - bows especially - and with the onset of cannons... Well, not a thought was ever given to these creatures, beyond the usual warnings to lone travelers about wild beasts.

But lately, reports began coming in.

A routine foray into the wilderness - to make sure the strange creatures made of air and rage were truly gone - was nearly annihilated by Lethe. It seems the usual technique of 'be even remotely competent' and 'have any gear whatsoever' was not up to the usual muster. A security memo was issued to train up on wild animal handling techniques, and not much more was said, for a time. Walls of spears at night would keep anyone at bay.

Well, not so much. It seems that after a few failed attacks, the Lethe started employing flanking tactics, and a subset of them developed specialized, hardened limbs for tearing down walls of spears.

A well-defended scholar was dispatched to study the problem. They had a front seat at the most terrible attack so far. Many Lethe - were they even Lethe, any longer? Writhing creatures of limbs and cunning - laid ambush, and after a long and grueling fight, absconded with the scholar (presumably to devour at leisure). Some of the remaining soldiers were ignored, and survived to relay the tale.

This was just the glimmering of a systematic problem, world over. Lethe were changing.

No longer relatively-simple wanderers, preying on the lost and lonely, the Lethe began to grow. To adapt. To transform. Each iteration stronger than the last. Most races noticed a slight upswing in local dangers, and a few lone, knowledgeable hermits going missing, later found slumped, breathing, yet mindless - if not devoured by opportunistic scavengers. Soon, however, the local increasingly-problematic Lethe population began to disappear. They were migrating. They were drawn to knowledge. To the greatest concentration of knowledge on Gaea. By underground tunnels they travel, the knowledge an irresistible beacon.

To Arsenal.

#####[tl;dr:]

No longer mere beasts, the Lethe began to arrive in force. An actual threat. The advanced knowledge of the Deva would spurn advancement in them, as well, and so, a monster is born that could always threaten, always challenge. It would take a significant failure indeed to completely succumb to their onslaught, but they will now always be there; Always be a threat; Always be advancing. Gone is the complacent safety of a society that has everything, for there is now a foe worthy of fighting with the best even the Deva can bring to bear. It would take some time for them to cross the huge gulfs of land beneath the sea, but sooner or later, they would arrive in force. Oblitus would yet feast.
